text:
pagerduty-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach on inference-runtime.continuous-batch path. Trigger at 1932109876. Severity: P2. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/serving/contbatch

mika: paging jamal and priya. Noting p95->p99 gap; p95 ~380ms, p99 ~2.1s in prod-us-west. Streaming sessions show token stalls mid-stream.

jamal: ack. Looking into batch formation logs. I see large batches with one or two seqs >2500 tokens combined with many short requests. Batch waiting for window to close.

priya: Is scheduler waiting for batch fullness rather than seqlen? We recently pushed throughput-oriented changes last week.

jamal: Right. Recent change bumped batch_target=128 and reduced max_wait_ms to 40ms, but the seqlen packing hasn't been updated. So long sequences make batch large in token count even if request count is low.

ops-bot: system: autoscaler note: no new allocs available in us-west for this class.

mika: Customer impact: support tickets from "voice-stream-prod" and "realtime-assist" reporting intermittent typing delays and one complaint about delayed first token. Escalated.

support-engineer: Confirmed two customers affected — both high-concurrency streaming apps. They saw delays for ~15 minutes starting at 1932109876.

priya: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) enable seqlen-aware packing heuristic 2) set streaming preemption so streaming requests get priority within batch 3) temporarily reduce batch_target for cont-batch workers handling streaming traffic. Which is fastest?

jamal: Fastest is to reduce batch_target and enable preemption flag. Seqlen-aware packing requires a small code change but we can flip a runtime flag if we have one.

mika: Can we route streaming-routes to a separate worker pool with max_batch_size=12? That would prevent mixing long offline batch jobs with low-latency streams.

jamal: Yes, we can add a routing override. I'll apply routing rule to divert streaming tag -> streaming-pool-canary. Then update config for that pool.

priya: Prep customer message template. Keep it short: "We observed intermittent streaming delays in us-west; engineering is rolling mitigations. Expect improvements in ~10-30 min. DM trace ids to support."

jamal: Applying quick fixes now: 
```
# quick runtime adjustments
set runtime.continuous_batch.batch_target=48 --group=prod-us-west
set runtime.streaming_pool.max_batch_size=12 --group=prod-us-west
set runtime.scheduler.preempt_for_streaming=true --group=prod-us-west
```
Executing on canary subset first.

ops-bot: deploy-job 6874 started by jamal at 1932109892.

jamal: Canary applied at 1932109896. Metrics: batch_token_count distribution shifted left, median batch tokens down ~40%. p99 in canary dropped to ~780ms, p95 ~320ms.

mika: Good. Start rolling to remaining allocs gradually. Watch for throughput regression.

priya: Rolling now and notifying affected customers. Support message sent.

support-engineer: Customer responses: appreciative, one asked if there's a permanent fix. We'll collect their workload traces if they consent.

jamal: Follow-up mitigation: enable temporary per-tenant long-request throttling for very long sequences to a batch-only pool to avoid them blocking streaming. This requires OS-level routing change but is low-risk.

priya: Please file post-incident action items: 1) implement seqlen-aware packing algorithm (cap cumulative tokens per batch) 2) add streaming isolation to default config 3) monitor batch composition metric and alert when long-request fraction > 5% 4) update runbook for similar incidents.

mika: I'll open the post-incident doc and assign owners. Also schedule a 1-hour deep dive tomorrow with infra and runtime teams.

jamal: Note: enabling streaming preempt increased scheduling CPU by ~3% but acceptable. We should track cost delta when rolling to all regions.

ops-bot: system: routing change applied at 1932109901.

mika: Handoff to night oncall (jamal) at 1932109905. If we see recurrence, escalate to P1. Otherwise, keep monitoring dashboards and collect traces for RFC. Thanks team. :rocket:
